rationale:
Evidence. Iterations 1 to 9 all ended off track on all 60 trials, each with one line-loss event and max_error of about 0.060 to 0.065 m. Tested changes that did not move this excursion: the +/-0.05 spread cut progress (iteration 2); ki 0.4 changed nothing (3); kd 0.15 gave a small gain (4); line_loss search_right matched last_direction exactly (5); base_speed 1.25 changed max_error by 0.001 to 0.004 m and gave the best raced score, 54.14 (6); kp 2.0 did not help (7); sensor_size 0.012 was neutral (8); and the spacing change to +/-0.025 gave 53.46 with max_error unchanged (9). Gains, speed, footprint, spacing and recovery direction are therefore exhausted. The feedback on iteration 9 says the spacing test should be followed by a body or drivetrain variable, but none of those has been changed yet.

The untested variable is forward sensor placement (y). All five sensors sit at y = 0.03, ahead of the axle. Because the robot turns about the axle, a sensor further forward sees the line earlier in each bend and reduces the lag between the error and the steering response. The excursion starts from an offset of about 0.05 m, where the 16 mm footprints lose the tape, so reacting earlier is the most plausible route to keeping the robot on the line. Moving the sensors to y = 0.06 (inside the allowed 0.08 maximum) is the single geometry change I can justify from the evidence.

Change. Against the best raced design (iteration 6: base_speed 1.25, kp 1.5, kd 0.15, ki 0, last_direction, x = +/-0.03 and +/-0.015 with 16 mm footprints), I change only sensor y from 0.03 to 0.06. I keep base_speed 1.25 because it is the best raced score, so this iteration's result is compared with 54.14. Everything else is unchanged.

Expected result: max_error falls below about 0.060 m on some seeds, or line_loss_events drops, with progress at least 0.165 (the iteration 6 s-bend level). The risk is that a longer lever changes the signal's lag or response in a way that makes the controller oscillate, which steering_oscillation will show.

Hypotheses and measurements. (1) Forward sensors reduce the bend excursion, so max_error and line_loss_events improve. (2) If max_error is unchanged, sensor position is not the limit, and the next candidate should test wheel_track 0.10 (a higher yaw rate per PWM difference) with the best controller. Measurements: max_error and line_loss_events per track, progress and completion_time (the run must cover the course with less loss), steering_oscillation (to check for jitter from the longer lever) and completion.
